text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Prime minister Romano Prodi is searching for a political deal to back the deployment of a security force for Albania. The government won a vote in the upper house but the lower Chamber of Deputies, where government lacks a majority after disagreement with hard-left communist allies, is due to vote on the Italian-led mission today. Greens party spokesman Manconi says centre-left alliance will not support opposition motion in lower house (all).

* Opposition Freedom Alliance intends to vote against government in Lower house vote on Albania, opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi rejects idea of reaching an agreement with the government and Alliance says government should back centre-right's motion (all).

* In an interview, hard-left Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti said a government crisis would not be his party's fault after Democratic Party of the Left leader Massimo D'Alema blamed Bertinotti for making government's survival depend on opposition's support (Corriere della Sera).

* Albania issued a strong diplomatic protest to Italy after Rome's deputy foreign minister Piero Fassino said the Italian government believed Albanian president Sali Berisha should leave office but would not push for his departure now (all).

* Giorgio Fossa, the president of Italian industrialists' association Confindustria, said recent budget deficit-cutting measures included in mini-budget would have a negative influence on Italy's industries. Prodi replied the government will go ahead with the extra 1997 budget (all).
* The board of investment bank IMI has authorised its executive committee to pursue negotiations which could lead to the group becoming a core shareholder of Istituto San Paolo di Torino (all).
* State electricity group Enel, due to be sold off later this year, is reportedly in talks with Deutsche Telekom over a joint venture to enter the cell phone market (Corriere della Sera).
* A report by national statistics institute Istat showed Italian retail sales rose 2.3 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 from the same quarter in the previous year (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
